Subject: Request: SDK deliverables + SLA exception for early integration

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to move forward with a POC. Legal flagged two items they need for our internal signoff:

1) A short delivery matrix that lists which SDK languages we get, expected GA date, and any runtime features that are "not supported" in the hosted plan (e.g., streaming, kv-cache pinning, quantized 4-bit).
2) A requested one-quarter SLA exception for 99.9% p99 latency for initial production (we understand this is an exception given our traffic profile).

Can you share a single-page deliverable that maps features to timeline and an internal contact for SLA exceptions? Contracts copied here.

Attachments: none from my side.

—Samir

Acme PaaS

Subject: Re: Request: SDK deliverables + SLA exception for early integration

Hi Samir — thanks, and excited to move this forward.

Marissa and I pulled together a draft delivery matrix (attached) and a one-page SLA exception request PDF for Contracts. The matrix lists current SDK surface (JS, Python, Go), estimated delivery windows for next 2 quarters, and a short callout on runtime capabilities.

Quick notes for your team:
- Hosted API supports streaming and KV caching today for standard models; some quantized variants are still on our roadmap and will require compatibility testing.
- The 99.9% p99 SLA exception can be scoped to the initial reserved capacity plan, but Platform will need details on qps and typical sequence lengths to confirm.

Action items:
1) Dev / Runtime: can you confirm whether streaming + kv-cache semantics for pinned sessions are fully supported under Dedicated vs Hosted, and any caveats? (cc: @dev.patel)
2) Platform: what short-term work would be required to give a contractual p99 commitment for one quarter? (cc: @karthik_iyer)
3) Samir/Contracts: if you can share the expected qps and 90th/95th seq length distributions, we can give a firmer answer.

I've attached delivery-matrix-v1.xlsx and redwood-sla-exception-request.pdf.

Thanks — I will follow up internally and share a single shepherded doc for Contracts.

Best,
Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK deliverables + SLA exception for early integration

Thanks for the context and the draft, Neha. I pulled a quick checklist for Runtime/Serving impact below — high level so Contracts and Acme can read it, then we can follow with technical notes.

Runtime compatibility checklist (notes):
- Streaming: supported for hosted API; p99 depends on model variant, payload size, and routing policy. For consistent p99 under high concurrency we recommend Dedicated or reserved pathway.
- KV Cache pinning: semantics exist today; pinned sessions increase memory footprint and reduce request multiplexing which reduces effective throughput. We need expected concurrency per pinned session to estimate capacity.
- Quantized models (4-bit): supported for some open models; there can be slight latency variance and occasional tokenization edge cases that require per-model validation.
- SDK surface: JS/Python are GA. Go SDK currently alpha; we can commit to beta in Q4 and GA in Q1 2027 depending on integration time.

Platform ask for SLA exception:
- To commit to a time-limited 99.9% p99 we need (a) qps profile, (b) seq length percentiles, (c) traffic shape (bursts), and (d) whether they will tolerate fallback routing to a lower-tier model in overload conditions.
- If Acme agrees to a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for the POC we can bound the p99 for one quarter with an SLO and a credit schedule.

Open technical questions for Acme (please provide):
- Expected concurrent pinned sessions and average TTL per session
- Percent of requests expecting streaming responses vs single-shot generation
- Tokenization edgecases: are there domain-specific tokens or long system prompts?

I can draft a short technical appendix for Contracts explaining the operational caveats. Happy to sync if you want a quick 20 min tech call.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@acme-paas.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK deliverables + SLA exception for early integration

Looping in Karthik for the contractual framing. From a product/PD perspective, two quick asks that will help Contracts and Acme decide:

1) If we offer a one-quarter p99 exception scoped to Dedicated, can Product provide an internal "compatibility flag" that documents which model variants we would allow for the commitment (so Contracts can enumerate in the Doc)? This avoids blanket language that forces product to cover unsupported variants.
2) For the SDK delivery timeline — Neha's matrix shows Go as Q4 beta; can we tighten to "target: mid-Nov" if we push an engineering resource? If yes, we should note the risk in the delivery matrix cell.

Karthik — do we have a standard contractual appendix template for time-limited SLA exceptions, or does Legal need a custom redline? If we have a template, I can ask Contracts to start pre-filling.

Thanks — happy to join a call to align.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — useful thread. Quick summary and next steps from my side: 

Summary:
- Delivery matrix (attached) v1 shared with Acme. Go SDK status: alpha -> target beta Q4; Product to confirm mid-Nov target and call out risk.
- Runtime: streaming and kv-cache are supported on Hosted today; Dedicated gives stronger p99 guarantees for heavy concurrency. Quantized model caveats noted.
- Contracts: we can scope a one-quarter 99.9% p99 exception if Acme provides traffic profile and accepts Dedicated/reserved pool pricing.

Next steps / owners:
- Acme (Samir): send qps profile + seq length percentiles and confirm whether fallbacks to lower-cost model are acceptable. (target: 2026-09-02)
- Dev: draft a 1-page technical appendix for Contracts that explains caveats and capacity assumptions. (owner: Dev Patel, target: 2026-09-03)
- Product: confirm whether Go SDK mid-Nov target is feasible or whether we keep Q1 GA. Add risk note to matrix. (owner: Karthik Iyer / Marissa, target: 2026-09-04)
- Contracts / Legal: pre-fill SLA appendix once Dev provides appendix and Product confirms model list. I will coordinate DocuSign routing. (owner: Contracts + Neha, target: 2026-09-07)

I uploaded the delivery matrix and initial SLA exception PDF to the Drive link above. Samir — please let me know if you prefer a 20 min tech sync tomorrow morning.

Best,
Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
